heading: AI & Compute Intelligence
subheading: The capex supercycle, silicon stack, foundation-model giants & the bubble debate

kpis.label: Amazon (~$220B), Alphabet ($195–205B), Microsoft (~$190B CY2026 / ~$255–260B FY2027 all-in), Meta ($130–145B) and Oracle (S&P models $90–95B FY2027) — combined $825–855B, unchanged this edition with no hyperscaler earnings until late October. Debt funding still sits near 32% of capex over the trailing twelve months (FactSet). New this week: the RBA (Oct 1) put hyperscalers' off-balance-sheet and vendor-financed obligations at an estimated US$1–1.5 trillion, funded by 20–30 year debt against hardware with 'uncertain economic lives'

kpis.sub: OPENAI'S BRIDGE ROUND VS. ANTHROPIC'S NOVEMBER IPO
kpis.label: Bloomberg reported Sept 29 that OpenAI is seeking at least $30B at a $1.4 trillion pre-money valuation (vs. $852B in March) as a bridge to a delayed IPO; Sam Altman has said a 2026 listing would be 'ill-advised', and annualized revenue is reported near $70B. Anthropic is pressing ahead: its marketing roadshow is reportedly targeted for the week of Nov 9 with trading before Thanksgiving (Nov 26) — later than the October timeline investors had expected — at an expected $1.8–2.0T valuation. Its prospectus reportedly projects $518B of cloud/compute spending commitments and a Founder LLC holding 50.1% of voting control via a single Class F share (reported; subject to change)

kpis.sub: BIS: SHARE OF AI INVESTMENT THAT IS AI-TO-AI; H1 2026 GLOBAL VC
kpis.label: The BIS (Bulletin 137, Oct 1) found that 55.2% of investment value flowing into 1,246 AI-supply-chain firms (2021–2025) came from other AI firms, and 46.4% of AI-to-AI deal value involved supply-chain relationships — the first central-bank quantification of circular financing, though the RBA noted aggregate leverage remains contained. Meanwhile H1 2026 global venture funding hit a record $510B (Crunchbase) with AI taking an estimated 70–80%, and corporate investors now account for ~88% of US AI venture deal value (PitchBook, July) with Nvidia the largest single corporate investor

kpis.sub: NVIDIA'S RECORD REPURCHASE INCREASE — BULLS AND BEARS BOTH POINT TO IT
kpis.label: Nvidia's board added $150B to its buyback authorization (the largest increase in history), leaving ~$235B through fiscal 2028; the stock trades near $231 (~+24% YTD, ~29x earnings) after Q2 FY27 revenue of $96.2B (+106%) and ~74.7% gross margin. Reported commitments for Nvidia-based capacity include up to $84.5B from Anthropic and xAI through 2029. Bears counter that Nvidia is deploying cash to prop up customers and itself at the same time; on Sept 27 it published data arguing A100/H100/B200 hardware holds value beyond accelerated depreciation schedules, and Michael Burry answered on Oct 2 with a 1960s computer-leasing bubble analogy

bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: The industry has now committed an estimated $3–4T to AI infrastructure against an annualized return requirement of roughly $600–800B in new profit (up from Sequoia's original $200B framework in late 2023), while actual AI-attributable revenue runs an estimated $50–150B a year — a gap that keeps widening as the top-5 hyperscaler 2026/FY27 capex total sits at $825–855B. For context, cloud computing's capex-to-revenue ratio at the same point in its adoption curve (2011) was roughly 2.4:1, far below today's multiple. The BIS's June 2026 annual report still names an AI-capex bust as one of its top three risks to global financial stability.

bear_case.title: AI's own architects sound the alarm
bear_case.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published "We Must Pace the Frontier" on Sept 12, arguing AI capability growth has accelerated "drastically faster" since summer 2026 — driven mainly by AI's growing ability to build the next generation of AI — and proposing independent safety evaluation, inter-lab coordination and international cooperation. OpenAI's Sam Altman and DeepMind's Demis Hassabis publicly backed the call; days later Palantir's Alex Karp went further, telling CNBC that frontier labs may need to be nationalized over "unlimited risk." The market reaction was real — chip names sold off while Meta, Alphabet and Microsoft rose — but skeptics note that a company mid-prep for a ~$2T IPO calling for the industry to slow down is also a moat-building and regulatory-capture argument, not purely an act of altruism.

bear_case.title: Rates are the transmission mechanism — but strength can still win the argument
bear_case.description: The 30-year Treasury eased slightly to ~5.36% on Sept 11 after touching its highest level since 2007 — still elevated as AI-linked debt issuance adds to bond-supply pressure. BofA estimates the surge in AI-related corporate debt sales has added roughly 0.3 percentage points to 10-year rates this year, and Nomura pegs hyperscaler borrowing alone at ~25% of net Treasury note/bond issuance to private investors. But Oracle's Sept 10 beat-and-raise, which sent the stock up ~15% on the week and has largely held since, kept the fundamental-demand side of the argument intact — a reminder the debate can swing hard in either direction week to week.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments off hyperscaler balance sheets, and on Oct 1 the RBA's Financial Stability Review estimated hyperscaler obligations via SPVs and vendor financing at US$1–1.5T, financed with 20–30 year debt against hardware of 'uncertain economic lives' — warning of potential losses for lenders if returns underperform. The RBA also noted aggregate leverage remains contained and balance sheets healthy. Oracle remains the starkest case (BBB-, FY26 FCF -$23.7B, S&P ~$42B FY27 deficit) despite genuinely strong Q1 FY27 results.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: The BIS (Bulletin 137, Oct 1) quantified it for the first time: 55.2% of investment value into 1,246 AI-supply-chain firms came from other AI firms, 28.7% of AI firms' invested value went to other AI firms, and 46.4% of AI-to-AI deal value involved supply-chain relationships (16.1% by count) — concentrated in large deals. Nvidia is reportedly in talks to anchor up to $10B of Anthropic's IPO, and Anthropic/xAI are cited for up to $84.5B of Nvidia-based capacity commitments. Michael Burry has called Nvidia's revenue 'majority circularly financed'. Counterpoint: the BIS framing is that this is a feature of a young supply chain rather than proof of systemic risk, and Broadcom's 3.5GW Google TPU deal for Anthropic is real non-Nvidia capacity being built.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years; Burry argues replacement cycles are really 2–3 years, understating depreciation by ~$176B across 2026–2028 and inflating Oracle's earnings by ~27% and Meta's by ~21%. On Sept 27 Nvidia published data arguing A100/H100/B200 hardware retains value beyond accelerated depreciation schedules, and on Oct 2 Burry replied by citing the 1960s computer-leasing bubble ('The Money Game'). Bull evidence: CoreWeave's CEO says H100 capacity was rebooked at ~95% of the original contract price and Nvidia says A100s are rented through 2029 — nine years after launch. Bear evidence: that is rental pricing for the best-contracted capacity, not proof the economic life of the whole installed base is 5–6 years.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Layoffs.fyi's tracker showed 128,536 tech workers cut across 299 companies in 2026 through Sept 10 (not refreshed this edition) — already exceeding all of 2025 — while a broader tracker (SkillSyncer, different methodology) counts 210,741 workers across 383 layoff events through Sept 20. xAI itself cut roughly 500 data-annotation staff (a third of that team) on Sept 12 as part of a stated pivot to "specialist AI tutors." The juxtaposition — record infrastructure spend, record layoffs, and AI labs restructuring their own workforces — keeps fueling the argument that AI economics lean partly on cost-cutting elsewhere, not purely on AI revenue.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took over 40% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total, and AI took 86% of all US venture dollars in H1 per PitchBook), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage and quantum sentiment at once. NVIDIA now sits at the center of deals spanning chips (TSMC, Broadcom), model hosting (Hugging Face), enterprise software (Palantir) and a potential anchor stake in Anthropic's IPO — a single company's balance sheet increasingly touches nearly every layer of this page, even as customers like Anthropic simultaneously build Google TPU alternatives. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters and Oracle's Sept 10 beat is a live example — some strategists call the bear case premature given actual demand signals.
